title: MTE4JNI: A Memory Tagging Method to Protect Java Heap Memory from Illicit Native Code Access
problem: Java Native Interface (JNI) allows native code to directly access Java heap via raw pointers, bypassing Java's safety guarantees and creating a significant attack surface on mobile platforms.
motivation: Android widespread adoption makes mobile security critical. JNI's unsafe pointer access undermines Java's memory safety model, threatening heap integrity.
method: MTE4JNI leverages ARM Memory Tagging Extension (MTE) to tag Java heap objects with metadata. Native JNI code access to tagged regions is monitored and enforced, preventing illicit pointer dereferences while maintaining performance. Runtime enforcement compares pointer tags against object tags.
key_novelty: First MTE-based approach to protect Java heap from unauthorized JNI native code access.
contributions: MTE-based runtime checking for JNI heap access
11× reduction in overhead vs. guarded copy (single-threaded)
Superior memory safety protection with practical overhead
limitations: Evaluation limited to ARM MTE-equipped devices; generalization to other ISAs not discussed.
